title: Height drops by at most the number of equations (Krull)
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $t\ge0$ an integer, $f_1,\dots,f_t\in R$, $J=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$ the ideal they generate, $\mathfrak P\subset R$ a prime ideal with $J\subseteq\mathfrak P$, and $\bar{\mathfrak P}=\mathfrak P/J$, a prime ideal of $R/J$. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of a commutative ring $A$ let $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\in\{0,1,2,\dots,\infty\}$ be the supremum of the integers $n\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\mathfrak q_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_n$ of prime ideals of $A$ with $\mathfrak q_n\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Then $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak P)\le\operatorname{ht}(\bar{\mathfrak P})+t$, the left side computed in $R$ and $\operatorname{ht}(\bar{\mathfrak P})$ in $R/J$.
